newsitem.title: CANADA: Ballard gains on Daimler deal.
newsitem.headline: Ballard gains on Daimler deal.

text.p: Shares in Ballard Power Systems Inc jumped on Monday on news of a deal between the fuel-cell maker and Germany's Daimler-Benz AG.
Ballard stock climbed 3.15 to 39.40 in Toronto.
Analysts said the agreement represented a milestone in Ballard's efforts to commercialize its emission-free fuel cell technology into an automobile power source.

Under the deal, Daimler-Benz will invest about C$450 million. It will invest C$198 million by contributing its fuel cell stack technology and fixed assets and C$142 million in cash in return for a 25 percent stake in Ballard.
The stake will consist of 5.6 million shares valued at C$35 each.
Daimler will also invest C$207 million, made up of its fuel cell system technology, related fixed assets and C$57 million in cash, into a new fuel cell engine company.
The new company will develop and commercialize fuel cell systems for use as automotive engines.
Ballard will invest C$103 million, made up of its technology, fixed assets and C$53 million in cash, into the new fuel cell engine company.
Daimler will own two-thirds of the fuel cell engine company and Ballard one-third.
The cells convert fuel such as methanol, natural gas or hydrogen into electricity without combustion using proton exchange membranes.
Combining systems such as a fuel processor, air supply, cooling and controls with the cells creates a fuel cell engine that can power vehicles.
